title: Serving runtime weekly update — kernel, KV cache, batching (2026-11-12)
content:
Summary:
- Focus this week: kernel micro-optimizations, KV cache correctness and eviction policy, and end-to-end batching improvements for medium-latency workloads.
- Goal: Stabilize kv-cache v2 behind feature flag and land batching throughput improvements to hit 15% lower p99 CPU on 1xA100 workloads.

Accomplishments:
1) Kernel work
   - Landed JIT kernel selection patch (PR #289) — reduces small-token attention overhead by ~8% in synthetic microbenchmarks.
   - Fixed a regression where fused softmax fallback triggered for sequence len <= 32 on Ampere. Regression tracked in SRV-4123.
   - Added per-core affinity hints to worker process startup; observed modest p50 latency reduction in local perf runs.

2) KV cache v2
   - Completed second pass on correctness tests: addressed stale reference bug when eviction and concurrent reads happen (root cause: race in refcount decrement).
   - Implemented LRU-approx eviction with TTL fallback; 3rd-party embedding workloads see ~12% reduced memory churn.
   - Feature-flag rollout plan: enable for 10% of traffic next week, increase to 50% after 72h if no regressions.

3) Batching and scheduler
   - Experimented with adaptive batch sizing (based on recent inter-arrival times). Early results: improved throughput by 10% for mixed short/long tail requests while keeping p99 within SLO.
   - Implemented backpressure gating to avoid queue amplification during autoscaling events. Needs more load testing.

Metrics & Observations:
- Local perf: 8% reduction in token CPU cost for small-context gen, 5% for medium-context.
- Staging end-to-end: p50 latency down 6ms, p99 steady (within 1% of baseline). Memory usage stable after kv-cache fixes.
- Canary (internal): at 10% traffic kv-cache v2 shows slight increase in tail latency on chat-heavy workload (identified to be due to a locking hotspot in cache lookup).

Blockers / Risks:
- Locking hotspot in kv-cache during high-concurrency chat workloads. Priya is working on replacing coarse-grain lock with sharded locks (SRV-4189).
- Backpressure gating needs integration tests for Dedicated autoscaler; until then, we risk queue buildup in rare burst scenarios.
- Kernel selection on older GPUs (T4) still falls back to slower path; need to add T4-specific heuristics before expanding rollout.

Plan for next week:
- Finish sharded-lock refactor for kv-cache and land in staging (owner: Priya).
- Run 48h canary with kv-cache v2 at 10% on production-like traffic, monitor p95/p99 and memory churn (owner: Michael).
- Expand adaptive batching experiments to Dedicated cluster (owner: Diego).
- Add T4 heuristic and run compatibility perf suite (owner: Lena).
- Document rollout runbook (canary checks, rollback steps) and add automated alerting for anomalous tail-latency.

Action items:
- Michael: kick off canary and add dashboard panels for cache hit/miss breakdown and lock contention.
- Priya: finish lock refactor and add unit tests for concurrent eviction cases.
- Diego: integrate adaptive batching with autoscaler simulation infra and run stress tests.
- Lena: add T4 kernel heuristic and run cross-GPU regression tests.

Notes & links:
- See SRV-4123 (Jira) for regression history and repro steps.
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/289 — kernel selection and softmax fixes.
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRV/kv-cache-design-v2 (kv-cache v2 design and rollout notes).

Open questions:
- What SLO guardrails should block kv-cache v2 expansion beyond 50%? (suggested: p99 increase > 5% or memory churn > 10% for 24h).
- Should we prioritize T4 heuristics before full rollout to Dedicated customers on T4-heavy fleets?

Appendix (short logs):

- 2026-11-11 14:40 — Staging canary reveals lock hotspots during simulated chat blast (T=3s inter-arrival).
- 2026-11-12 08:00 — Sharded-lock approach prototyped, rough data looks promising (reduced contention by ~70% in microbench).
